doc.title: Dick Spottswood interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 13, 2023

title: Record collecting prices and a Blind Willie McTell record
summary: He says blues were throwaway music in the 1920s and a McTell record recently sold for over $100,000.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: Well yeah they sure tried. And today their children and grandchildren are collecting them all over again. So I mean it’s the story of the blues to start with. It was the throwaway music in the 20s and somebody is reputed to have paid in excess of 100 Gs for a Blind Willie McTell record recently. That’d give anybody the blues.
It’s like buying a piece of art, isn’t it?

Well it’s certainly a hundred thousand dollars worth of music but it represents a new high in record collecting. It represents record collecting really graduating from an affordable class into something only people with incomes like Eric Clapton and Paul McCartney can afford. You know? It means more and more records are going to end up in fewer and fewer places as people like you and me lack the resources to compete with them.
